feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 3 (+/-0.05 m, 16 mm, mass 0.7 kg, kp 2.5, kd 0.2) removed oval line loss (0 events, from 1 to 2 on earlier designs) but still logged 1 loss each on the S-bend and slalom. Every run ended off_track with max_error about 0.064 m, and progress stayed at 0.11 to 0.17, so runs are lost early on the first sharp bends. Body_width cannot move the off-track limit, which stays at 0.06 m. Iteration 1 showed that kp 3.0 raised oscillation to 0.186, so the lever left is dynamic: mass. I have kept the iteration 3 controller and footprints unchanged so the mass effect is isolated. The mass effect itself is untested. Decide the next step from the next race as follows. If line_loss_events is still 1 on the S-bend or slalom at 0.6 kg, the loss is not geometric: do not change geometry again, and check the controller's line_loss handling and start position first. If line_loss_events is 0 on all tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, mass is not enough: try 0.5 kg, and separately test wheel_track 0.12 m for more turn authority. If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed. Progress is the current limit, not completion time, so do not change wheel_radius before runs finish.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks and max_error still approaches 0.06 m at mass 0.6 kg, try mass 0.5 kg, since the 0.7 to 0.6 kg step is the first test of whether lower yaw inertia cuts bend overshoot (iteration 3 at 0.7 kg logged max_error about 0.064 m).

If max_error stays near 0.06 m with no line loss after the mass change, try wheel_track 0.12 m for more differential turn authority. The 0.06 m off-track limit cannot be moved by body_width, so this is the geometry lever left for the bends.
Only if runs complete and completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, try wheel_radius 0.035 m. Iteration 3 has progress of only 0.11 to 0.17, so top speed is not yet the constraint.
